author: Cinna Davis with OpenAI Codex
statement: An enumerated pairwise-independent finite-field index family and polynomial-evaluation coefficient family give fewer than 64 max(q,P)^2 P^2 candidate rows per round, q < 2m; each support of size at least m/P is rejected with probability at least 1/12, enabling 8n greedy rounds under the source counting oracle. This compresses preprocessing but does not improve the selected SAT bound.
remaining_obligations: Independent review of the pairwise-index proof and complete oracle composition
Independent review of the all-size construction, coefficient family and oracle cost composition
Implement and independently replay the cited constant-degree expander construction and rational spectral checker
Find a changed contraction or preprocessing contract where candidate compression affects a dominant term
No improved alpha or full new SAT algorithm is claimed
